=== FOUR FINDINGS OF T802'S OWN, all from the census, all in spec.md section 14 rows 9-12 ===

9 (MAJOR) THE COOLDOWN MERGE WAS THREE OF FOUR, AND THE OMITTED ONE IS THE ONE WITH THE INCIDENT. ORC-POL-4 and ORC-GATE-2 both merge heal (T504) + dispatch (T536) + window (T628/T677). A fourth exists: untracked/fleet-keeper.cooldown, tested by fleet-keeper.sh's cooldown_set() as os.listdir(dir) + basename membership. Because it is a FILE'S EXISTENCE it carries no owner, no reason and no expiry - all three of which ORC-POL-2 requires of every policy entry. It is GLOBAL: no family, model or row scope. Its unreadable-directory branch returns True, so a permissions fault idles the whole fleet as a dead-man's switch. Nothing expires it.
AND IT IS LIVE, NOT HISTORICAL. Measured 2026-08-23T19:40Z: keeper process ALIVE (pid 99956, ppid 1, elapsed 3d04h), last dispatch 2026-08-20T18:25:26Z (T554 -> claude-fable-5), and 8,747 CONSECUTIVE 'cooldown flag set - no new dispatches' ticks since - about 73 hours - while 21 rows sit dispatchable. Section 3 calls this 'the 2.5-day silent global cooldown of 2026-08-20->23'; it is now 3 days and still counting, because the flag has no expiry to lapse and no dashboard row to make it visible. A merge that left this out would have preserved both the fourth place to look AND the incident. Both ids amended. Its boolean is the one state whose arithmetic deliberately does NOT survive the merge: a state with no expiry cannot be a state of a machine whose defining property is that pauses lapse loudly.

10 (MAJOR) ORC-PLAN-3 STEP 3 IS NOT A MOVE. The step reads 'rendering moves to managent'. Measured: the five sections ORC-DASH-4 specifies (keeper, pauses, window+appetite, benched, queue) and the five untracked/watch-fleet.sh actually renders (PROGRESS, CONCERNS, RECENT, DONE, OPEN) have an EMPTY INTERSECTION. So step 3 is a build plus a deletion, and neither the spec nor the audit noticed. Two consequences: T738's omission rule, T739's fill-the-screen rule and T799's footer work all attach to sections ORC-DASH-4 does not keep, so they must be re-expressed or they are lost rather than carried; and the current pane answers 'what is happening to my TASKS' while the specified pane answers 'what is happening to my FLEET'. Both are wanted. Recommendation on record: render both groups as one pane under the omission rule. This is the one open question for the operator that is a preference rather than evidence.

11 (MAJOR) THE 0-9 APPETITE DIAL EXISTS IN NO TRACKED SOURCE FILE. ORC-POL-3 says the dial is per-model 0-9 and that section 7c.11's mechanics 'carry over unchanged'. There is nothing to carry: the dial lives only in orchestration-layer-spec.md section 7c.11 PROSE. What exists is TWO per-family CATEGORICAL tables, and they DISAGREE - fleet-keeper.sh:325 has family 'ollama' = SPEND (quota handled by a separate model-level DENY) while main.zig:313 has family 'ollama-cloud' = OFF; Fable is 'fable' in one and 'claude-fable' in the other. So the same model resolves to a different family NAME and, for the three ollama models, a different APPETITE depending on which reader is asked. This is an 11TH MULTI-WAY JOB, absent from roadmap section 6's table of ten. Recommendation recorded as [design-open]: build the dial and derive the family word by stated floor thresholds, because the categorical form cannot express section 7c.11's monotone back-pressure at all (there is no 'slightly less') - and it must be chosen explicitly rather than by whichever table step 1 happens to port.
Sub-finding, latent: fleet-keeper.sh has NO oxalpha row at any granularity, so family_of('oxalpha') -> 'other' -> APPETITE.get('other','SPEND') -> SPEND. The keeper NEVER honoured RESERVED for oxalpha; before the 2026-08-23 operator ruling it would have auto-dispatched an identity-sealed model, and it is only ACCIDENTALLY correct now. Step 1's rule must be: unknown model -> refusal, never a default appetite. A default that silently permits is the D036 class this sprint exists to kill.

12 (MEDIUM) ARB-4's MECHANISM IS HALF-BUILT ALREADY. Store-write identity is std.c.getenv("MANAGENT_TASK_ID") - the spoofable-by-unsetting source ORC-ARB-4 forbids - while managent ALREADY parses `ps -axo pid=,ppid=,pgid=,uid=,etime=,rss=,state=,comm=` for the host-guard/reap path. The parent-PID chain ORC-ARB-4 wants is therefore already read; it is simply not consulted for store-write authority. Recorded so step 2 extends that reader instead of building a second process table.
